sections.skill: Keep passwords and keys out of prompts and avoid shared accounts

questions.prompt: What is an access key (API key)?

choices.text: A key that opens your front door
A secret code that lets software use your account
A public code anyone may share
A list of the shortcut keys on a keyboard

questions.correct_answer: A secret code that lets software use your account
questions.intro: PASSWORDS, ACCESS KEYS (also called API keys: secret codes that let software use a paid service on your account) and recovery codes are SECRETS: anyone who has them can act as you. Never paste them into a chat or a prompt, even to "help debug" a problem; describe the problem and use a placeholder like [API_KEY] instead. Do not put secrets inside code you share or upload. Avoid SHARED ACCOUNTS: if several people use one login, you cannot tell who did what, saved history may be visible to everyone, and one person's mistake affects all. Use two-step verification where available.
questions.feedback: Keys let software act on your account.

sections.skill: Compare passwords and keys with house keys

questions.prompt: Why not tape your house key to the door?

choices.text: Doors do not have locks
Keys are too heavy for tape
Anyone could use it to get in
Tape is illegal

questions.correct_answer: Anyone could use it to get in
questions.intro: A house key lets anyone who holds it walk in as if they live there. You would not hand it to a stranger, tape it to the front door, or post a photo of it online, because a photo can be used to copy it. Passwords and access keys are the same: whoever has them can act as you. Pasting a key into a chat or code you share is like posting a photo of your house key. If you think a copy got out, you change the lock.
questions.feedback: Exposed keys grant access.

sections.skill: Respond to exposed secrets and protect recovery

questions.prompt: Mia accidentally pasted an API key into a chat. What should she do first?

choices.text: Wait to see if anything happens
Revoke the key and create a new one
Ask the tool to forget the key
Delete the chat and do nothing else

questions.correct_answer: Revoke the key and create a new one
questions.intro: If a secret is exposed, act quickly: change the password or REVOKE (cancel) the key at its source and create a new one, then check the account for activity you did not do. Deleting the chat where you pasted it is not enough, because copies may exist. Also protect account RECOVERY: a recovery email or phone number someone else controls can let them take over your account. Unexpected messages asking for a code "to verify your account" are a common trick; real services do not ask you to read codes to them.
questions.feedback: Cancel the exposed secret at its source.

questions.prompt: After replacing an exposed password, what should you also do?

choices.text: Use the same password elsewhere

Turn off two-step verification
Check the account for activity you did not do
